chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he
said regarding a bequest which none had witnessed except a woman: he permitted the testimony of the woman for one quarter of the bequest, in accordance with the measure of her testimony.

key_terms.الربع: The quarter — one-fourth; in this context, the portion of the bequest validated by one female testimony
key_terms.شهادة: Legal testimony/witnessing — the formal evidence given before a judge
key_terms.وصية: Bequest/will — a person's final instructions for the distribution of their estate after death

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about a woman's testimony in a bequest witnessed only by her?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issued a ruling that when only a single woman witnessed a bequest (will/testament), her testimony is valid and sufficient to establish one-quarter of the bequest's value. This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that a woman's testimony is weighted at half that of a man's for certain matters, so one female witness substantiates one quarter (half of a half share) rather than the full amount. The hadith addresses a specific scenario in Islamic inheritance law where witnesses to a dying person's bequest are limited.
